paragraphs.title: Opening: The Lord Speaks to Moses and Aaron

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: Who spoke in the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “The Lord spoke,” so the Lord is speaking.

easy.question: To whom were the words spoken?
easy.explanation: The words were spoken to Moses and Aaron.

medium.question: What can we understand from the Lord addressing both Moses and Aaron?
answers: The message was intended for both
medium.explanation: The verse names both Moses and Aaron as the recipients.

medium.question: In the phrase “saying unto them,” who does “them” refer to?
medium.explanation: “Them” refers to Moses and Aaron, who were named immediately before.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Moses and Aaron spoke, then the Lord answered
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron to give them instructions
The Lord commanded the people before speaking to Moses
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron, and then gives them his message.

challenge.question: Why does the verse name Moses and Aaron?
answers: To identify who received the Lord’s message
To say that they wrote the verse
To announce that they were kings
challenge.explanation: Naming them clearly identifies the recipients of the Lord’s words.

challenge.question: What does “saying” at the end of the verse suggest?
answers: The speech ended without a message
The Lord was about to give them specific words
Moses and Aaron had already answered
challenge.explanation: “Saying” introduces the content that the Lord was about to communicate.

challenge.question: What detail is easy to miss in the verse?
answers: The Lord addressed two people together
The Lord addressed only one person
The verse does not identify the recipients
challenge.explanation: The verse addresses both Moses and Aaron, not just one person.

questions.question: Why does the verse name Moses and Aaron?
answers: To identify who received the Lord’s message
To say that they wrote the verse
To announce that they were kings
questions.explanation: Naming them clearly identifies the recipients of the Lord’s words.

questions.question: What does “saying” at the end of the verse suggest?
answers: The speech ended without a message
The Lord was about to give them specific words
Moses and Aaron had already answered
questions.explanation: “Saying” introduces the content that the Lord was about to communicate.

questions.question: What detail is easy to miss in the verse?
answers: The Lord addressed two people together
The Lord addressed only one person
The verse does not identify the recipients
questions.explanation: The verse addresses both Moses and Aaron, not just one person.

easy.question: Who are Moses and Aaron told to address?
easy.explanation: The command begins, “Speak unto the children of Israel.”

easy.question: What kind of animals are discussed?
easy.explanation: These verses discuss beasts, or land animals.

easy.question: What is one sign of an animal that may be eaten?
easy.explanation: The verse includes animals that chew the cud.

medium.question: What must a beast have to be eaten according to these verses?
answers: It must live only on land
It must divide the hoof and chew the cud
It must be large and strong
medium.explanation: Both signs are required: a divided hoof and chewing the cud.

medium.question: What does “chew the cud” mean here?
answers: Bring food back up to chew it again
medium.explanation: Chewing the cud means bringing food back up for further chewing.

medium.question: What is the status of an animal with only one of the two signs?
answers: It may be eaten only at night
medium.explanation: The verse requires both signs together.

challenge.question: What does “whatsoever” suggest at the beginning of the rule?
answers: The rule applies to one animal only
The rule applies broadly to animals meeting the description
The rule applies only to large animals
challenge.explanation: The wording presents a general rule for every qualifying beast.

challenge.question: What does the list of the two signs show?
answers: Only the first sign is needed
The second sign cancels the first
challenge.explanation: The divided hoof and chewing the cud are presented together as the requirements.

challenge.question: What does “that shall ye eat” refer to?
answers: Only an animal that chews the cud
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the beast described as having both required signs.

questions.question: What does “whatsoever” suggest at the beginning of the rule?
answers: The rule applies to one animal only
The rule applies broadly to animals meeting the description
The rule applies only to large animals
questions.explanation: The wording presents a general rule for every qualifying beast.

questions.question: What does the list of the two signs show?
answers: Only the first sign is needed
The second sign cancels the first
questions.explanation: The divided hoof and chewing the cud are presented together as the requirements.

questions.question: What does “that shall ye eat” refer to?
answers: Only an animal that chews the cud
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the beast described as having both required signs.

easy.question: Which sign is missing in the camel?
answers: It does not divide the hoof
It does not chew the cud
It does not live on land
easy.explanation: The camel chews the cud but does not divide the hoof.

easy.question: Which animal has a divided hoof but does not chew the cud?
easy.explanation: The swine divides the hoof but does not chew the cud.

easy.question: What may not be done with the unclean animals named here?
answers: They may not be touched at all
Their flesh may not be eaten and their carcasses may not be touched
easy.explanation: The verse forbids eating their flesh and touching their carcasses.

medium.question: Why is the camel unclean?
answers: It has only one of the two signs
medium.explanation: The camel chews the cud but lacks the divided hoof.

medium.question: What does “chew the cud” describe?
answers: Bringing swallowed food back up to chew it
medium.explanation: The expression describes bringing food back up for further chewing.

medium.question: What do the coney and hare have in common in this passage?
answers: They do not chew the cud
They are described as chewing the cud but not dividing the hoof
medium.explanation: Both are described as chewing the cud without having a divided hoof.

challenge.question: What do the examples of the camel and swine demonstrate?
answers: Both signs are required; one is not enough
Only small animals can be clean
Chewing the cud matters more than the hoof
challenge.explanation: The camel has one sign and the swine has the other, yet both are unclean.

challenge.question: What chiefly distinguishes the swine from the camel?
answers: The swine does not chew the cud, but the camel does
The swine divides the hoof, but the camel does not
The swine is unclean, but the camel is clean
challenge.explanation: The swine has the divided hoof; the camel does not.

challenge.question: How does verse 8 relate to verses 4–7?
answers: It permits the animals listed earlier
It summarizes the ban on eating their flesh and touching their carcasses
challenge.explanation: After listing the animals, verse 8 gives the general prohibition.

questions.question: What do the examples of the camel and swine demonstrate?
answers: Both signs are required; one is not enough
Only small animals can be clean
Chewing the cud matters more than the hoof
questions.explanation: The camel has one sign and the swine has the other, yet both are unclean.

questions.question: What chiefly distinguishes the swine from the camel?
answers: The swine does not chew the cud, but the camel does
The swine divides the hoof, but the camel does not
The swine is unclean, but the camel is clean
questions.explanation: The swine has the divided hoof; the camel does not.

questions.question: How does verse 8 relate to verses 4–7?
answers: It permits the animals listed earlier
It summarizes the ban on eating their flesh and touching their carcasses
questions.explanation: After listing the animals, verse 8 gives the general prohibition.

easy.question: What two signs must a water creature have to be eaten?
easy.explanation: The verse permits creatures with fins and scales.

easy.question: Where are these creatures found?
answers: On land and in the hills
easy.explanation: The passage mentions waters, seas, and rivers.

easy.question: What is said of a creature without fins and scales?
answers: It may be eaten on holidays
It is an abomination and may not be eaten
easy.explanation: Creatures lacking both signs are called an abomination.

medium.question: Why may a creature with fins and scales be eaten?
answers: It meets the condition set by the Lord
It is larger than other creatures
medium.explanation: Fins and scales are the stated requirements.

medium.question: What does “move in the waters” describe?
answers: Creatures that move through the water
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to living creatures that move in the water.

medium.question: How are clean and unclean water creatures treated differently?
answers: Both may be eaten, but only one may be sold
The unclean may be eaten if it comes from the sea
The clean may be eaten, while the unclean may not be eaten and is regarded as an abomination
medium.explanation: The passage permits the clean creatures and rejects the others.

challenge.question: A water creature with fins but no scales is, according to the passage:
answers: Unclean, because both signs are required
Clean, because one sign is enough
Clean only if it lives in a river
challenge.explanation: The permission is given to creatures with both fins and scales.

challenge.question: Which expression is repeated to emphasize the seriousness of the prohibition?
challenge.explanation: “An abomination” is repeated for creatures lacking the required signs.

challenge.question: What does the mention of seas and rivers show?
answers: The rule applies only to land animals
The rule concerns only fresh water
The rule covers creatures in different bodies of water
challenge.explanation: Both seas and rivers are included in the rule.

questions.question: A water creature with fins but no scales is, according to the passage:
answers: Unclean, because both signs are required
Clean, because one sign is enough
Clean only if it lives in a river
questions.explanation: The permission is given to creatures with both fins and scales.

questions.question: Which expression is repeated to emphasize the seriousness of the prohibition?
questions.explanation: “An abomination” is repeated for creatures lacking the required signs.

questions.question: What does the mention of seas and rivers show?
answers: The rule applies only to land animals
The rule concerns only fresh water
The rule covers creatures in different bodies of water
questions.explanation: Both seas and rivers are included in the rule.

easy.question: What is the main prohibition in these verses?
answers: The listed birds may not be eaten
Birds may not be kept at home
easy.explanation: The passage lists birds that are not to be eaten.

easy.question: Which bird is mentioned in verse 15?
easy.explanation: Verse 15 mentions every raven after its kind.

easy.question: Which creature appears at the end of the list?
easy.explanation: The list ends with the bat.

medium.question: Which bird is mentioned immediately after the raven?
medium.explanation: The list continues with the ostrich after the raven.

medium.question: What does “after his kind” mean in this passage?
answers: According to its kind or species
According to the color of its feathers
medium.explanation: The phrase extends the rule to the relevant kind or species.

medium.question: Which statement best summarizes the list?
answers: All the creatures live in water
All the listed creatures may not be eaten
medium.explanation: The passage identifies every creature in the list as an abomination not to be eaten.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by calling the creatures an abomination and saying they may not be eaten?
answers: They are regarded as abhorrent and forbidden as food
They are permitted only at certain times
challenge.explanation: The two statements reinforce their forbidden status.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the bat being listed among flying creatures?
answers: The bat is a bird of prey
The passage uses a practical category of flying creatures, not modern scientific classification
The bat lives only where birds live
challenge.explanation: The passage groups flying creatures without using modern biological categories.

challenge.question: Which animal is introduced with “every,” emphasizing the whole kind?
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “Every raven after his kind.”

questions.question: What is emphasized by calling the creatures an abomination and saying they may not be eaten?
answers: They are regarded as abhorrent and forbidden as food
They are permitted only at certain times
questions.explanation: The two statements reinforce their forbidden status.

questions.question: What can we understand from the bat being listed among flying creatures?
answers: The bat is a bird of prey
The passage uses a practical category of flying creatures, not modern scientific classification
The bat lives only where birds live
questions.explanation: The passage groups flying creatures without using modern biological categories.

questions.question: Which animal is introduced with “every,” emphasizing the whole kind?
questions.explanation: The passage says, “Every raven after his kind.”

easy.question: What is said about flying creatures that go on all four?
easy.explanation: The passage calls them an abomination.

easy.question: What condition allows some flying creeping things to be eaten?
answers: They have legs above their feet for leaping
easy.explanation: The permitted creatures have legs above their feet for leaping.

easy.question: Which creature is listed among those that may be eaten?
easy.explanation: The locust is included in the permitted list.

medium.question: Why are legs and the ability to leap both mentioned?
answers: They identify the special permitted group
They show that the creatures live in mountains
medium.explanation: These features identify the exceptions to the general prohibition.

medium.question: What does “to leap” mean in this passage?
medium.explanation: The word refers to jumping on the earth.

medium.question: How does the instruction change from verse 20 to verses 21–22?
answers: A general prohibition is followed by specific exceptions
A general permission is followed by a total prohibition
The subject changes from fish to birds
medium.explanation: Verse 20 gives the general rule, and the next verses name permitted exceptions.

challenge.question: What does “yet” at the beginning of verse 21 indicate?
answers: The rule applies only at night
There is an exception to the general prohibition
challenge.explanation: “Yet” introduces the permitted exception.

challenge.question: What could mislead someone reading quickly?
answers: Only creatures with the specified signs are permitted
Every creature that jumps is forbidden
challenge.explanation: The permission depends on the special legs and ability to leap, not merely on having four feet.

challenge.question: Why does the list say “after his kind”?
answers: The permission includes the relevant kinds or species
Only one creature of each kind may be eaten
challenge.explanation: The wording extends the permission to the kinds represented by each listed creature.

questions.question: What does “yet” at the beginning of verse 21 indicate?
answers: The rule applies only at night
There is an exception to the general prohibition
questions.explanation: “Yet” introduces the permitted exception.

questions.question: What could mislead someone reading quickly?
answers: Only creatures with the specified signs are permitted
Every creature that jumps is forbidden
questions.explanation: The permission depends on the special legs and ability to leap, not merely on having four feet.

questions.question: Why does the list say “after his kind”?
answers: The permission includes the relevant kinds or species
Only one creature of each kind may be eaten
questions.explanation: The wording extends the permission to the kinds represented by each listed creature.

easy.question: How long is a person unclean after touching a carcass?
easy.explanation: The passage says the person is unclean until evening.

easy.question: What must someone carrying a carcass do?
easy.explanation: The person carrying it must wash his clothes.

easy.question: What kind of animal is described in verse 27?
answers: An animal that goes on its paws
easy.explanation: Verse 27 refers to animals that go on their paws.

medium.question: What two results follow from carrying a carcass?
answers: Washing clothes and uncleanness until evening
A sacrifice and seven days of uncleanness
Washing in water and immediate cleansing
medium.explanation: The carrier must wash his clothes and remains unclean until evening.

medium.question: What does “carcase” mean here?
medium.explanation: A carcass is the body of a dead animal.

medium.question: Why is the animal in verse 26 unclean?
answers: It lacks the required clean-animal signs
medium.explanation: The verse describes an animal that does not properly meet the required signs.

challenge.question: What is the practical difference between touching and carrying a carcass?
answers: Carrying it also requires washing one’s clothes
challenge.explanation: Both cause uncleanness until evening, but carrying also requires washing clothes.

challenge.question: Which detail defines the animals in verse 27?
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically describes animals going on their paws.

challenge.question: What does the repeated phrase “until the evening” show?
answers: Uncleanness is temporary and ends at evening
challenge.explanation: The repeated phrase shows that this uncleanness is time-limited.

questions.question: What is the practical difference between touching and carrying a carcass?
answers: Carrying it also requires washing one’s clothes
questions.explanation: Both cause uncleanness until evening, but carrying also requires washing clothes.

questions.question: Which detail defines the animals in verse 27?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically describes animals going on their paws.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase “until the evening” show?
answers: Uncleanness is temporary and ends at evening
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase shows that this uncleanness is time-limited.

paragraphs.title: Unclean Creatures That Creep on the Earth

easy.question: Which animal is named first in verse 29?
easy.explanation: The weasel is the first animal named.

easy.question: Which animal comes after the weasel?
easy.explanation: The mouse follows the weasel in the list.

easy.question: Which name appears in verse 30?
easy.explanation: The ferret is named in verse 30.

medium.question: What does “after his kind” mean in this list?
answers: According to its kind or species
medium.explanation: The phrase includes the kinds or species belonging to the animal named.

medium.question: What do all the animals in verses 29–30 have in common?
medium.explanation: The passage introduces them as unclean creeping things.

medium.question: How is the list arranged?
answers: It begins in verse 29 and continues in verse 30
It is repeated twice in the same order
medium.explanation: Verse 30 continues the list begun in verse 29.

challenge.question: How many different animal names appear in the complete list?
challenge.explanation: There are three names in verse 29 and six in verse 30, making nine.

challenge.question: Which animal is explicitly followed by “after his kind”?
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “the tortoise after his kind.”

challenge.question: What should we cautiously infer from the order of the names?
answers: The last name is most important
The passage gives a list without assigning importance to the order
The animals are ordered by size
challenge.explanation: The passage lists the animals but does not state that the order reflects importance or size.

questions.question: How many different animal names appear in the complete list?
questions.explanation: There are three names in verse 29 and six in verse 30, making nine.

questions.question: Which animal is explicitly followed by “after his kind”?
questions.explanation: The passage says, “the tortoise after his kind.”

questions.question: What should we cautiously infer from the order of the names?
answers: The last name is most important
The passage gives a list without assigning importance to the order
The animals are ordered by size
questions.explanation: The passage lists the animals but does not state that the order reflects importance or size.

easy.question: Who becomes unclean according to verse 31?
answers: Anyone who touches a dead creeping thing
easy.explanation: The verse says that whoever touches them in death becomes unclean.

easy.question: How long does the person remain unclean?
easy.explanation: The verse says the person is unclean until evening.

easy.question: Which item is mentioned in verse 32?
easy.explanation: The verse mentions a vessel of wood, along with clothing, skin, and sack.

medium.question: What happens to a vessel on which a dead creeping thing falls?
medium.explanation: Anything on which one of the dead creatures falls becomes unclean.

medium.question: What is a “sack” in this context?
medium.explanation: The word appears with clothing and skin and refers to coarse material or a sack.

medium.question: What is the stated process for an unclean vessel?
answers: Put it in water, leave it until evening, and it becomes clean
medium.explanation: The verse says it must be put into water and remain unclean until evening.

challenge.question: What causes the uncleanness described here?
answers: The existence of an earthen vessel
A dead creature falling onto the vessel
challenge.explanation: The rule applies when one of the dead creatures falls onto the vessel.

challenge.question: What does the required washing in water suggest?
answers: Ordinary cleaning alone is not enough
The vessel must be made of gold
challenge.explanation: The verse gives a specific process for cleansing the affected vessel.

challenge.question: What does “any of them” refer to?
challenge.explanation: It refers to the unclean creatures whose dead bodies may fall onto objects.

questions.question: What causes the uncleanness described here?
answers: The existence of an earthen vessel
A dead creature falling onto the vessel
questions.explanation: The rule applies when one of the dead creatures falls onto the vessel.

questions.question: What does the required washing in water suggest?
answers: Ordinary cleaning alone is not enough
The vessel must be made of gold
questions.explanation: The verse gives a specific process for cleansing the affected vessel.

questions.question: What does “any of them” refer to?
questions.explanation: It refers to the unclean creatures whose dead bodies may fall onto objects.

easy.question: What happens when an unclean creature falls into an earthen vessel?
easy.explanation: The verse says that whatever is in it becomes unclean.

easy.question: What must be done with the earthen vessel?
easy.explanation: The verse commands, “ye shall break it.”

easy.question: What kind of vessel is mentioned?
easy.explanation: The verse begins by mentioning an earthen vessel.

medium.question: Why does what is inside the vessel become unclean?
answers: Because an unclean creature fell into it
Because it was made of earth
medium.explanation: The uncleanness follows the fall of the unclean creature into the vessel.

medium.question: What does “break it” mean here?
medium.explanation: The command requires the vessel to be broken.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Something falls into the vessel, its contents become unclean, and the vessel is broken
The vessel breaks, then something falls into it
The contents become unclean, then the vessel is filled and closed
medium.explanation: The verse presents those three events in that order.

challenge.question: What activates the uncleanness rule?
answers: The mere existence of an earthen vessel
An unclean thing falling into the vessel
challenge.explanation: The rule is triggered when an unclean thing falls into the vessel.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the command to break the earthen vessel?
answers: Washing or ordinary cleaning is not enough
The vessel must be made of gold
challenge.explanation: The prescribed remedy is to break the vessel, not merely wash it.

challenge.question: What does “any of them” refer to in this context?
challenge.explanation: It refers to the unclean creatures whose falling causes the uncleanness.

questions.question: What activates the uncleanness rule?
answers: The mere existence of an earthen vessel
An unclean thing falling into the vessel
questions.explanation: The rule is triggered when an unclean thing falls into the vessel.

questions.question: What can we infer from the command to break the earthen vessel?
answers: Washing or ordinary cleaning is not enough
The vessel must be made of gold
questions.explanation: The prescribed remedy is to break the vessel, not merely wash it.

questions.question: What does “any of them” refer to in this context?
questions.explanation: It refers to the unclean creatures whose falling causes the uncleanness.

easy.question: What happens to edible food when water comes upon it?
easy.explanation: The verse says that food touched by such water becomes unclean.

easy.question: What must be done to an oven or cooking range on which a carcass falls?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the oven and range must be broken down.

easy.question: What is said about a fountain or pit with plenty of water?
easy.explanation: The passage specifically says that such a fountain or pit shall be clean.

medium.question: What is the difference between seed before and after water is put on it?
answers: The first remains clean, while the second becomes unclean if a carcass falls on it
The first is unclean, while the second is clean
medium.explanation: Dry seed remains clean, but seed moistened before contact with a carcass becomes unclean.

medium.question: What does “carcase” mean in this passage?
answers: The dead body of the animal
medium.explanation: A carcass is the dead body of an animal.

medium.question: Why does the seed in verse 38 become unclean?
answers: Water had first been put on it
medium.explanation: The verse makes the order clear: water is put on the seed, and then the carcass falls on it.

challenge.question: What is presented as an exception that remains clean?
answers: A fountain or pit with plenty of water
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically declares a fountain or water-filled pit clean.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from comparing verses 34 and 38?
answers: Moistening food or seed can make it subject to uncleanness from a carcass
challenge.explanation: Food and seed that have received water become unclean when touched by a carcass.

challenge.question: What special practical instruction is given for an unclean oven or range?
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says that such cooking equipment must be broken down.

questions.question: What is presented as an exception that remains clean?
answers: A fountain or pit with plenty of water
questions.explanation: The passage specifically declares a fountain or water-filled pit clean.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from comparing verses 34 and 38?
answers: Moistening food or seed can make it subject to uncleanness from a carcass
questions.explanation: Food and seed that have received water become unclean when touched by a carcass.

questions.question: What special practical instruction is given for an unclean oven or range?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says that such cooking equipment must be broken down.

paragraphs.title: The Carcass of a Clean Animal

easy.question: Who becomes unclean when touching the carcass of a clean animal?
easy.explanation: The verse says that whoever touches the carcass becomes unclean.

easy.question: How long does the person remain unclean?
easy.explanation: The passage says the person is unclean until evening.

easy.question: What must someone who eats from the carcass do?
easy.explanation: The person who eats from it must wash his clothes.

medium.question: What is the difference between touching the carcass and eating or carrying it?
answers: The eater and carrier must also wash their clothes
Only the person who touches it remains unclean
Only the person who touches it must leave the camp
medium.explanation: The passage adds the requirement to wash clothes for eating or carrying the carcass.

medium.question: What does “the carcase thereof” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the dead body of the animal.

medium.question: What do the person who eats and the person who carries the carcass have in common?
answers: Both wash their clothes and remain unclean until evening
medium.explanation: The same requirements are stated for both the eater and the carrier.

challenge.question: What follows specifically from eating or carrying the carcass?
answers: An explicit duty to wash one’s clothes
A more serious uncleanness than touching
challenge.explanation: The passage adds washing clothes to the uncleanness caused by eating or carrying.

challenge.question: Why does the verse say the animal is one that may be eaten?
answers: To say every animal may be eaten
To identify an ordinarily edible animal that has died
To say that the animal is still alive
challenge.explanation: The case concerns an animal normally fit for food but now dead.

challenge.question: What does “until the evening” show about the eater and carrier?
answers: Washing is required, but uncleanness lasts until evening
challenge.explanation: Washing is required, yet the stated period of uncleanness continues until evening.

questions.question: What follows specifically from eating or carrying the carcass?
answers: An explicit duty to wash one’s clothes
A more serious uncleanness than touching
questions.explanation: The passage adds washing clothes to the uncleanness caused by eating or carrying.

questions.question: Why does the verse say the animal is one that may be eaten?
answers: To say every animal may be eaten
To identify an ordinarily edible animal that has died
To say that the animal is still alive
questions.explanation: The case concerns an animal normally fit for food but now dead.

questions.question: What does “until the evening” show about the eater and carrier?
answers: Washing is required, but uncleanness lasts until evening
questions.explanation: Washing is required, yet the stated period of uncleanness continues until evening.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition against Eating Creeping Things

easy.question: What may not be done with a creature that creeps on the earth?
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly forbid eating such creatures.

easy.question: Where are these creatures said to creep?
easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly says they creep on the earth.

easy.question: What may happen to someone made unclean by these creatures?
easy.explanation: The passage warns that contact with them can make a person unclean.

medium.question: Why are creatures that go on the belly, four feet, or many feet grouped together?
answers: They all creep on the earth and may not be eaten
They all live only in water
medium.explanation: Different forms of movement are included under the category of creatures creeping on the earth.

medium.question: What does “abomination” mean in “it shall not be eaten”?
medium.explanation: The context shows that an abomination is detestable and forbidden as food.

medium.question: What is the main order of ideas in the verses?
answers: Animals are described, then the earth is created
Eating is forbidden, then uncleanness is warned against
medium.explanation: The passage first forbids eating them and then warns against becoming unclean through them.

challenge.question: What do the animals in verse 42 have in common despite moving differently?
answers: They are all creatures creeping on the earth
They all fly above the earth
They all walk on two feet
challenge.explanation: The verse includes different forms of movement but groups them as earth-creeping creatures.

challenge.question: What additional warning is given in verse 43?
answers: Some creeping things may be eaten
Contact or involvement with them can make a person unclean
They must be used in temple service
challenge.explanation: Verse 43 adds a warning about becoming unclean, not merely about eating.

challenge.question: Why is “creepeth upon the earth” repeated?
answers: To say all animals live only on land
To emphasize the class of creatures moving along the earth
challenge.explanation: The repetition focuses the prohibition on creatures that move along the ground.

questions.question: What do the animals in verse 42 have in common despite moving differently?
answers: They are all creatures creeping on the earth
They all fly above the earth
They all walk on two feet
questions.explanation: The verse includes different forms of movement but groups them as earth-creeping creatures.

questions.question: What additional warning is given in verse 43?
answers: Some creeping things may be eaten
Contact or involvement with them can make a person unclean
They must be used in temple service
questions.explanation: Verse 43 adds a warning about becoming unclean, not merely about eating.

questions.question: Why is “creepeth upon the earth” repeated?
answers: To say all animals live only on land
To emphasize the class of creatures moving along the earth
questions.explanation: The repetition focuses the prohibition on creatures that move along the ground.

paragraphs.title: Holiness and the Exodus from Egypt

easy.question: Who says, “I am holy”?
easy.explanation: The Lord declares that he is holy.

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to be?
easy.explanation: The passage commands them to be holy.

easy.question: From which land did the Lord bring up Israel?
easy.explanation: The Lord says he brought them out of Egypt.

medium.question: Why must the Israelites be holy?
medium.explanation: The command is based on the Lord’s own holiness.

medium.question: What does “to be your God” mean here?
medium.explanation: The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt to be their God.

medium.question: What connection does the passage make between the Exodus and holiness?
answers: The Lord brought them out to be their God, so they must be holy
medium.explanation: The Exodus established the Lord’s special relationship with Israel and grounds the call to holiness.

challenge.question: Why does mentioning the Exodus strengthen the command to be holy?
answers: The Lord redeemed Israel, so they are obligated to live as his people
challenge.explanation: The Exodus highlights Israel’s special relationship and obligation to the Lord.

challenge.question: What does the repeated statement “I am holy” emphasize?
answers: The Lord’s holiness is the basis for Israel’s holiness
The Lord is speaking about two different gods
challenge.explanation: The repetition makes the Lord’s holiness the central reason for the command.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by “neither shall ye defile yourselves”?
answers: The command applies only to leaders
These practices can defile the person himself
challenge.explanation: The wording concerns the people’s own purity, not merely external objects.

paragraphs.title: The Purpose of the Laws of Uncleanness and Cleanness

easy.question: What creatures are discussed in the summary?
easy.explanation: The summary mentions beasts, birds, water creatures, and creatures that creep on the earth.

easy.question: What distinction does the Lord command Israel to make?
easy.explanation: The passage says to distinguish between the unclean and the clean.

easy.question: Which creatures are said to move in the waters?
answers: Every living creature that moves in the waters
easy.explanation: The summary includes every living creature that moves in the waters.

medium.question: What is the purpose of these laws?
answers: To distinguish among kinds of animals
To teach people how to raise animals
To tell the story of creation
medium.explanation: The laws help Israel distinguish between clean and unclean animals and between edible and forbidden animals.

medium.question: What does “creepeth upon the earth” describe?
answers: Moving or crawling along the earth
medium.explanation: The phrase describes creatures that move along the ground.

medium.question: How does verse 47 continue verse 46?
answers: It explains the purpose of the classifications
It changes the subject to the Israelites
It removes the distinctions among animals
medium.explanation: Verse 46 identifies the animals covered, and verse 47 explains the purpose of distinguishing them.

challenge.question: What can we infer from distinguishing both clean and unclean animals and edible and forbidden animals?
answers: These are two related but distinct classifications
They are exactly the same distinction
Only unclean animals are forbidden as food
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both ritual status and suitability as food as distinct categories.

challenge.question: What important detail is easy to miss in the list of creatures?
answers: It includes creatures in water and creatures on land
challenge.explanation: The summary includes beasts, birds, water creatures, and earth-creeping creatures.

challenge.question: What structure appears across the two verses?
answers: A question followed by an answer
A story followed by a proverb
First the subject of the laws, then their purpose
challenge.explanation: The first verse identifies the creatures covered, and the second explains the purpose of the rules.
